title: Daily Dependence on Grace
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Daily dependence on grace means relying on God’s mercy, strength, and help for the ongoing Christian life. Believers are saved by grace and must also grow, endure, repent, serve, and obey by grace.
summary: Daily dependence on grace means relying on God’s mercy, strength, and help for the ongoing Christian life. Believers are saved by grace and must also grow, endure, repent, serve, and obey by grace.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the source of grace for His people. From His fullness believers receive grace upon grace, and apart from Him they cannot live the Christian life God commands.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Grace is not only the beginning of the Christian life. The same God who saves by grace sustains His people by grace. Believers need His help for repentance, obedience, endurance, service, and growth.

Daily dependence on grace rejects both pride and despair. Pride says, “I can do this in my own strength.” Despair says, “I can never change.” Grace teaches believers to come boldly to the throne of grace for mercy and help.

God’s grace trains His people. It does not leave them unchanged or careless. The grace that saves also teaches believers to renounce ungodliness and live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers quietly return to self-effort after receiving salvation by grace. They try to mature by pressure, shame, comparison, or willpower alone. This leads to exhaustion or pride.

This doctrine reminds the weak and weary that God gives grace for today. The Christian life is not self-powered religion, but ongoing dependence on Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God for grace every day. Bring your weakness, temptations, failures, responsibilities, and needs to Him. Serve diligently, repent honestly, and obey faithfully, but do it as one who depends on Christ’s strength rather than personal ability.
